text.p: Nigeria's electoral authorities and the five registered political parties on Sunday agreed to carry remaining activities of the transition programme scheduled for this year early in 1997 .

"It was unanimously resolved that the outstanding activities of the third and fourth quarters of 1996 be shifted to the first quarter 1997," said a statement signed by electoral authorities and leaders of the parties after a meeting in the capital Abuja.
"Such activities would be concluded between the 10th of February and the 31st of March 1997," it added.

Military ruler General Sani Abacha last year announced a plan to return Africa's most populous nation to civilian rule by October 1998, which Nigerian opposition groups and Western governments have criticised as too long.
Under the previous plan, registration and production of voters list and conducting municipal elections had been scheduled for completion by this month.

"The meeting recognised that as much as these changes have become necessary, they do not negate the basic objective of the transition programme, which terminal date remains 1st October, 1998," it said.
"(The electoral commission) would publish an appropriate programme of activities to include the carryover activities along with those earlier scheduled for the 1st quarter 1997."
